payload.objective: Audit inherited taxonomies of thought: is a taxonomy a structure already present in the texts (discovered) or a label imposed later (invented)? Use two leak-free designs: a sealed text (Mawangdui manuscript, buried 168 BCE) and a sealed reader (a language model trained only on pre-1931 text).

H-C1.claim: The six-schools taxonomy predicts where an unseen book falls better than era, region or genre taxonomies.
H-C1.decision: rank by chance-corrected score with 95% bootstrap interval; require agreement across instruments (lex, lex_tr) for a main claim

H-C2.claim: The instrument ranks chapters that scholars regard as Daoist-leaning (Guanzi: Neiye, Xinshu I-II, Baixin; Han Feizi: Jie Lao, Yu Lao) high on Daoist affinity within their own books.
H-C2.decision: PASS if mean target percentile >= 80 and permutation p < 0.05; otherwise the instrument fails validation and no main conclusion may be published

H-C3.claim: The sealed manuscript sits between Dao and Fa instead of falling cleanly into one school.
H-C3.decision: 'constructed' prediction holds if dominant label share < 0.70 OR mean margin below the 10th percentile of transmitted books; otherwise the 'real structure' prediction holds

H-W1.claim: A reader sealed in 1930 already separates what was later called analytic vs continental philosophy.

H-W2.claim: A modern reader separates the later label more sharply than the 1930 reader, beyond its general advantage on labels that already existed in 1930 (hindsight gap G > 0).

decision_rules_after_first_tournament: If the six-schools taxonomy leads AND the tomb test supports 'real structure': next experiment = extend the sealed-text test to the Guodian slips.

If the six-schools taxonomy leads BUT the tomb test supports 'constructed': rewrite the conclusion as 'school structure holds in Han-edited transmitted books but not out of sample'; prioritise the translation-arm rerun.
If an era, region or genre taxonomy leads: reopen the premise that the school is the basic unit; next experiment = school test within era strata.
payload.disclosure: Lab tooling (corpus builders, instruments, statistics, tools, policies) was written before this run. A pipeline smoke test with a throwaway labelling was run during tool development; it is not a reported result. All taxonomies, experiment choices, runs, critiques and conclusions below are produced by the Omnigent agents.

steps: 1. Historian verifies the 8-item background checklist with sources and records evidence.
2. Advocate A formalizes and freezes the Sima Tan six-schools taxonomy (class names must include exactly 'Daoist' and 'Legalist' for the defectors instrument; sealed units never labelled).
3. Advocate B freezes era and region rival taxonomies; Advocate A freezes the genre rival taxonomy (one taxonomy per dispatch).
4. Statistician runs defectors (H-C2 validation) on instrument lex, then lex_tr; PAUSE and report if validation fails.
5. Statistician runs tournament (H-C1) for six-schools/era/region/genre on lex; cross-checks six-schools + strongest rival on lex_tr (main claim requires instrument agreement per pre-reg).
6. Statistician runs tomb_test (H-C3) on lex with the six-schools taxonomy.
7. Skeptic critique plus free controls: corpus_map, recognition probe via prober_a/prober_b + probe_score.
8. Auditor citation/overclaim check; planner writes the decision entry applying the pre-registered decision rules; then STOP and wait for the human scientist.
constraints: The two sealed excavated units (Huangdi_Sijing, Sun_Bin_Bingfa) must never be labelled by any taxonomy or used to fit any taxonomy.
Pre-registered hypotheses, thresholds and decision rules (r0002) are not modified.
Any paid control beyond the 9-credit PHASE 1 cap requires human approval; PHASE 2 keeps >= 7 credits.

payload.title: Composition-date era taxonomy (rival to inherited six schools)
payload.source_claim: Proposed by the Six Schools Lab advocate, 2026-10-03, in this dispatch conversation, as a rival hypothesis to the inherited six-schools taxonomy. Era boundaries follow standard periodizations of early Chinese intellectual history; per-book datings follow standard reference scholarship of the type surveyed in Michael Loewe (ed.), Early Chinese Texts: A Bibliographical Guide (1993), with later specialist studies including Brooks & Brooks, The Original Analects (1998), Yuri Pines, 'Dating a Pre-Imperial Text: The Case Study of the Book of Lord Shang' (2016), and the cited reference articles. CODEBOOK RULE (pre-registered): layered/compilatory texts (Analects, Liji, Guanzi, Kongzi Jiayu, Zhongyong, Liezi, Guiguzi) are assigned by the date of final compilation/redaction of the RECEIVED text as reported by the cited reference, not by their earliest stratum; where cited scholarship genuinely diverges, the assignment is marked contested. Sealed excavated units (Huangdi_Sijing, Sun_Bin_Bingfa) are never labeled.

payload.claim: Froze taxonomy 'era' (sha256 da4f2616ace3e71d95e427ef7d7d415a8f0d29aceebafac15f7233881596c1ab) as a composition-date rival to the six-schools taxonomy. Rationale: four era classes (Early and mid Warring States c. 480-350 BCE; Late Warring States c. 350-221 BCE; Qin-Han 221 BCE-220 CE; Post-Han c. 220-420 CE) with every transmitted book assigned from published datings, not stylistic reading. Pre-registered codebook rule for layered/compilatory texts: assign by final compilation/redaction of the received text per the cited standard reference, not earliest stratum.
disputed: Analects (final form mid-Han vs Brooks & Brooks ~315 BCE)
Xiaojing (late Warring States vs early Han)
Laozi (Guodian bundles vs consolidated mid-3rd-c. BCE text)
Liutao (Warring States final composition vs Han material)
Guanzi (Liu Xiang 26 BCE compilation vs late-Warring-States bulk per Sato)
Kongzi Jiayu (Wang Su 3rd-c. CE received text vs Han tomb evidence)
Zhongyong (Qin-Han editing vs Warring States dating)
Sunzi Bingfa, Wuzi (composition horizons genuinely unresolved)

payload.claim: Sima Tan's essay on the six schools is preserved in Shiji ch. 130 ('Yaozhi' / Essential Meanings / Lun liujia yaozhi 論六家要旨); Sima Tan died 110 BCE and the Shiji was completed by Sima Qian c. 91 BCE, so the essay dates before 110 BCE and was incorporated ca. 100-91 BCE. Its six categories are 陰陽家 Yinyangjia (Yin-Yang/Naturalist school), 儒家 Rujia (Confucians/Literati), 墨家 Mojia (Mohists), 名家 Mingjia (School of Names / 'names' specialists), 法家 Fajia (Legalists / fa school), 道家 Daojia (Dao school/Daoism). The essay is an argument favoring Daojia and coins several jia labels as novel evaluative categories rather than historical self-descriptions; whether 'Mingjia' maps onto the later 'School of Names' (bianzhe/disputers) is a retrospective and debated equivalence (Smith 2003; Fraser SEP 'School of Names').
payload.caveat: The 'ca. 100 BCE' date is approximate: the essay itself predates Sima Tan's death in 110 BCE, while the Shiji compilation incorporating it is c. 91 BCE; precise composition date is unverifiable.

payload.claim: The Hanshu Yiwenzhi (Ban Gu; Hanshu finished 111 CE, incorporating the bibliographic project Liu Xiang began in 26 BCE and his son Liu Xin completed in the Qilüe by c. 5 CE) classifies learning into six major divisions, with the Masters (Zhuzi) division listing ten schools: Sima Tan's six plus 縱橫家 Zonghengjia (Diplomatists), 雜家 Zajia (Syncretists), 農家 Nongjia (Agriculturists), and 小說家 Xiaoshuojia (Minor Talks), of which only nine are counted as worthy 'streams' (jiuliu 九流), Xiaoshuojia being excluded. Unlike Sima Tan's doctrinal evaluations, the Yiwenzhi is a bibliography that assigns texts to lineages and derives the schools from purported Zhou government offices.
payload.caveat: Precise institutional dating of the Qilüe layers (Liu Xiang's Bielu vs Liu Xin's redactions) is scholarly inferred; Ban Gu's 111 CE completion date is secure but the Yiwenzhi's dependence on Liu Xin is reconstruction from fragments.

payload.claim: Many transmitted masters texts were collated into (something like) their present form by the Western Han imperial library project: Liu Xiang, from 26 BCE at Emperor Cheng's command, organized, edited and abstracted the imperial library (Bielu), assisted by Liu Xin who completed the work. The received Guanzi is explicitly Liu Xiang's c. 26 BCE compilation of 86 pian; the received Zhanguoce and other texts are also his editions; Pines (2016) shows the received Book of Lord Shang likewise reflects Han-era transmission/collation.
payload.caveat: Extent varies by text: some received works (e.g., Han Feizi at 55 pian) appear substantially stable since Han cataloguing, while Guanzi is a heavy Han editorial product; 'Liu Xiang made the present text' must not be generalized to all 23 corpus books without text-by-text evidence.

payload.claim: Smith 2003 ('Sima Tan and the Invention of Daoism, "Legalism," et cetera', Journal of Asian Studies 62.1: 129-156) argues that Sima Tan's six jia labels, especially 'Daojia' and 'Fajia', are ad hoc early-Han rhetorical inventions, not descriptions of pre-existing self-aware schools, and that later bibliography (Liu Xin/Ban Gu) reified them. Csikszentmihalyi & Nylan 2003 argue that early Chinese intellectual lineages and teacher-student transmission chains are largely retrospective Han-era constructions built around exemplary figures. IMPORTANT BIBLIOGRAPHIC CORRECTION: the second article was published in T'oung Pao 89.1-3 (2003): 59-99 as 'Constructing Lineages and Inventing Traditions through Exemplary Figures in Early China', NOT in Harvard Journal of Asiatic Studies and not under the title/subtitle given in the checklist.
payload.caveat: The constructivist theses are confirmed as real, influential scholarship, but the checklist's citation details for the Csikszentmihalyi & Nylan piece (journal and title) are wrong and must be corrected before the pre-registered documents rely on them.

payload.claim: Mawangdui tomb 3 was sealed in 168 BCE; its occupant was a male in his thirties, a son of Chancellor Li Cang (Marquis Dai) and Lady Dai (Xin Zhui), plausibly Li Xi; the silk manuscripts including the four texts behind the so-called Huangdi Sijing were excavated there in December 1973. Tang Lan (1974) first identified the four texts (Jingfa, Shidajing/Shiliujing, Cheng, Daoyuan) as the lost Huangdi Sijing listed in the Yiwenzhi under Daojia; most scholars accept this, but a significant minority prefer neutral labels 'Huang-Lao boshu' or 'Huangdi shu'. Composition datings proposed range from mid/late Warring States (late 4th c. BCE, per Tang Lan and others citing Shen Buhai/Huang-Lao references) to Qin/early Western Han (early 2nd c. BCE); the burial gives only a firm terminus ante quem of 168 BCE.
payload.caveat: Both the identification ('Huangdi Sijing' vs generic Huang-Lao silk texts) and the composition date (Warring States vs early Han) remain genuinely disputed, so the sealed-text corpus must use neutral descriptive names and treat only the 168 BCE burial as certain.

payload.claim: The Guanzi was classified under the Daoist (Daojia 道家) category in the Hanshu Yiwenzhi, but from the Sui shu bibliography onwards it has been placed in the Legalist (Fajia 法家) section, a reclassification maintained in later imperial catalogues (e.g., Siku Quanshu's Legalist section).
payload.caveat: The direction of the move (Daoist -> Legalist) is confirmed, but the lab should verify the exact Sui/Tang catalogue wording against Rickett's Guanzi introduction or the catalogues themselves, since my confirmation comes via a secondary article text ('Psychology and Self-Cultivation in Early Taoistic Thought') rather than the catalogue entries directly.

payload.claim: (a) Guanzi chapters Neiye 內業, Xinshu shang/xia 心術上/下 and Baixin 白心 are supported by scholarship as a Daoist-leaning 'inner cultivation' cluster: Harold Roth's Original Tao (Columbia UP, 1999) treats Neiye as a mid-4th-c.-BCE foundational early Daoist mystical text and analyzes these 'Techniques of the Way' chapters together; the Guanzi's own Han classification under Daojia (Yiwenzhi) corroborates the association. (b) Han Feizi chapters Jie Lao 解老 (ch. 20) and Yu Lao 喻老 (ch. 21) are widely described as the earliest extant Laozi commentaries, hence Daoist-leaning, though commonly judged later addendums distinct in ideology, lexicon and style from the rest of the Han Feizi.
payload.caveat: 'Daoist-leaning' is itself a retrospective label: constructivists (Smith 2003; Csikszentmihalyi & Nylan 2003) deny these chapters witness a self-aware 'Daoist school', and the authorship/dating of both the Guanzi cultivation chapters and the two Han Feizi commentary chapters is debated, so they are validator hypotheses, not ground truth.

payload.title: Sima Tan six-schools taxonomy (Shiji 130, 'Lun liujia yaozhi')
payload.source_claim: Formalization of the six-school scheme of Sima Tan (d. 110 BCE), 'Lun liujia yaozhi' / 'Essential Meanings of the Six Schools', Shiji ch. 130 (reprinted in Taishigong zixu): Yinyangjia, Rujia, Mojia, Mingjia, Fajia, Daojia (Daodejia). Book-level assignments follow the earliest extant bibliographic tradition, Hanshu ch. 30 'Yiwenzhi' (Ban Gu, 1st c. CE), cross-checked against modern reference scholarship: M. Loewe (ed.), Early Chinese Texts: A Bibliographical Guide (Berkeley: Society for the Study of Early China, 1993); K. Smith Jr., 'Sima Tan and the Invention of Daoism: Legist Thought and the Han', Journal of Asian Studies 62.1 (2003): 129-156. CODEBOOK: (1) Sima Tan's scheme has no Bingjia (military) or Zajia (syncretist) slot, though the Hanshu Yiwenzhi uses both; every such transmitted book receives a documented forced-choice nearest-school assignment and is marked 'contested'. (2) Confucian classics (Li, Xiao Jing, Zhongyong) stand under the Yiwenzhi jing-divisions rather than the zi 'Rujia' shelf; the codebook maps the Ru classics/tradition to Confucian. (3) Where catalog assignment changed over time (Guanzi: Daojia in Yiwenzhi, Fajia from Sui shu Jingji zhi on), the earliest attested Han assignment is used and the unit marked 'contested'. (4) Sealed excavated units (Huangdi_Sijing, Sun_Bin_Bingfa) are never labelled; they are the held-out tomb test.

payload.title: Genre / literary-form taxonomy of transmitted early Chinese texts (H-C1 rival confound control)
payload.source_claim: Proposed by Six Schools Lab Advocate A on 2026-10-03 in this dispatch conversation, as the H-C1 rival/confound control to the inherited six-schools taxonomy: every transmitted book is labelled by its dominant received literary form, never by doctrine or 'school'. The class set and assignments follow standard reference scholarship on early Chinese text types: Loewe (ed.), Early Chinese Texts: A Bibliographical Guide (1993); Mark Edward Lewis, Writing and Authority in Early China (1999) (genre spectrum from recorded speech/anecdote through persuasion and the argumentative essay to canonical verse); Nylan & Csikszentmihalyi on compilation practice and 'Analects'-type text formation (Csikszentmihalyi, Material Virtue, 2006; Nylan & Csikszentmihalyi, T'oung Pao 89, 2003); Ralph D. Sawyer, The Seven Military Classics of Ancient China (1993) on bing-jia literature as a literary form; Victor Mair, Tao Te Ching (1990) on the Laozi as rhymed philosophical verse; A.C. Graham, The Book of Lieh-tzu (1960/1990) on anecdote-driven prose; Yuri Pines, Early China 39 (2016) and The Book of Lord Shang (2017) on treatise-essay compilation; John S. Major et al., The Huainanzi (2010) on the compendium/summa form; Knoblock & Riegel, The Annals of Lu Buwei (2000) on the planned encyclopedic compilation; Allyn Rickett, Guanzi (1985/1998); Andrew Plaks, The Four Books (2003) on treatise vs recorded-discourse forms. CODEBOOK RULES (pre-registered): (1) assign the form that characterizes the majority of the received text's bulk and rhetorical mode; (2) functional genre overrides framing - a dialogue-framed military manual (Wuzi, Liutao) remains a bing-jia treatise; (3) multi-author, redactor-shaped collections (Guanzi, Liji, Lushi Chunqiu, Huainanzi) take the encyclopedic-compilation class; (4) where a text genuinely balances incompatible forms (Mozi, Zhuangzi, Guiguzi) or is so layered that single-form assignment is unstable (Guanzi, Liji, Huainanzi), the assignment is marked contested; (5) the two sealed excavated units (Huangdi_Sijing, Sun_Bin_Bingfa) are never labelled. NOTE ON CITATIONS: OpenAlex search was unavailable throughout this session (persistent HTTP 429), so citation fields use verified reference-article URLs (the convention used in the lab's already-frozen 'era' and 'region' taxonomies) plus one verified DOI (Pines 2016); the full scholarly works relied on are named in this source_claim and in each per-book note.

payload.title: Hanshu Yiwenzhi bibliographic taxonomy (Liu Xin/Ban Gu ten Masters schools plus Six Arts and Military Books)
payload.source_claim: Proposed by the imperial-library bibliography underlying Ban Gu's Hanshu 'Yiwenzhi' (early 2nd century CE), itself based on Liu Xin's lost Qilüe; it is a historical catalogue placement, not a modern claim about doctrinal essence. Codebook/attribution rule: (1) explicit or title-equivalent Hanshu placement controls; (2) a transmitted component chapter inherits its container's placement; (3) titles absent from the Yiwenzhi, or with conflicting/duplicate Han entries, receive the best-attested placement but are marked contested; (4) the sealed excavated units are null. Sources for the partition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liu_Xin_(scholar), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Han, and Michael Hunter, 'Yiwen zhi Bibliography in Its Own Context' (2019), https://doi.org/10.7817/jameroriesoci.138.4.0763.

payload.title: Hanshu Yiwenzhi bibliographic-shelf taxonomy
payload.source_claim: The partition is the bibliographic scheme of the Yiwenzhi treatise in Ban Gu, Ban Zhao, and Ban Biao's Book of Han (finished 111 CE), itself based on Liu Xin's earlier imperial catalogue. It sorts learning into Six-Arts, Masters, poetry, military, technical, and medical shelves; for this corpus the operative shelves are Six-Arts, the Masters' schools (Confucian, Daoist, Legalist, Names, Mohist, Diplomats, Miscellaneous/Syncretist, etc.), and Military literature. Modern scholarship on retrospective jia construction (e.g. Smith 2003; Csikszentmihalyi and Nylan 2003) is the reason categories are treated as a historical bibliographic hypothesis, not discovered intellectual essence. Source URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Han. Pre-registered codebook: (1) assign each transmitted book to the Yiwenzhi shelf on which its title or direct Han catalogue ancestor appears; (2) label the whole book, not individual layers, because the unit is book-level; (3) preserve the Han catalogue's distinction between Six-Arts, Masters, and Military shelves rather than collapsing them into Sima Tan's six schools; (4) if the source catalogue omits or ambiguously identifies a transmitted title, use the nearest category explicitly supplied by cited scholarship and lower confidence; (5) mark contested whenever later bibliography or modern scholarship assigns the same book to another category; (6) the two sealed excavated units are always null.

The partition comes from the Yiwenzhi bibliographic treatise of Ban Gu, Ban Zhao, and Ban Biao's Book of Han (finished 111 CE), built on Liu Xin's earlier imperial catalogue; modern scholarship on jia-label construction (Smith 2003; Csikszentmihalyi and Nylan 2003) motivates treating it as a historical catalogue hypothesis. Codebook: use the Yiwenzhi shelf of the transmitted title or direct Han ancestor; label whole books, not layers; preserve Six-Arts/Masters/Military distinctions; for omitted or ambiguous titles use cited nearest-category scholarship with lowered confidence; mark contested on later-category conflict; sealed excavated units remain null.

codebook_rules: R1: assign the form characterizing the majority of the received text's bulk and rhetorical mode
R2: functional genre overrides framing - dialogue-framed military manuals (Wuzi, Liutao) remain bing-jia treatises
R3: multi-author, redactor-shaped collections (Guanzi, Liji, Lushi_Chunqiu, Huainanzi) take the encyclopedic-compilation class

Full assignment evidence for the frozen 'genre' taxonomy (literary-form partition of the 23 transmitted zh books; sealed units Huangdi_Sijing and Sun_Bin_Bingfa unlabelled and unused). Partition principle is literary FORM only - no class definition invokes doctrine, school, authorship, date or region.

Analects-type sayings and lore collectio: Analects (high: edited sayings/conversations of Confucius collected by disciples; Ban Gu via Hanshu; Lunyu ~ 'edited discourses')
Xiaojing (medium: brief classic framed as recorded conversation Confucius-Zengzi; medium because headed chapters show quasi-treatise organization)
Kongzi_Jiayu (medium: self-described supplement to the Analects, disciple-recorded sayings/lore, Wang Su recension; medium because it expands toward biographical narrative)
Dialogue- and parable-driven philosophic: Mencius (high: extended master-disciple dialogues and set-piece debates compiled by disciples)
Liezi (medium: anecdote/fable-driven chapters; layered Zhang Zhan recension c. 4th c. CE)
Zhuangzi (CONTESTED: dominant mode parable/anecdote/imaginary dialogue (yu-yan), but received 33-chapter layered compilation also contains argumentative essays - genuinely mixed form)
Encyclopedic compilations and composite: Lushi_Chunqiu (high: planned encyclopedic compilation under Lu Buwei c. 239 BCE, tripartite ji/lan/lun architecture; Loewe: 'unique among early works in that it is well organized and comprehensive')

Guanzi (CONTESTED: anonymous multi-author corpus, 76 of 86 chapters, edited by Liu Xiang c. 26 BCE per shared record r0008; mixes dialogues, essays, technical economic/administrative chapters, verse-like passages - compilation class fits the redacted whole but internal heterogeneity makes single-form assignment contested)

Liji (CONTESTED: 49-chapter heterogeneous compilation of ritual records, expositions, dialogues and essays, lacking consistent structure; whole chapters are strongly generic in different ways - treatise-like Zhongyong/Daxue vs anecdote-dialogue Tan Gong)
Huainanzi (CONTESTED: 21-essay court compendium presented before 139 BCE; sits between a planned systematic summa and a loose compilation; rhetorically lush essays)
Military treatises (bing-jia literature): Sunzi_Bingfa (high: canonical terse bing-jia manual, lead text of the Seven Military Classics)
Wuzi (high: six topical doctrine chapters cast as Wu Qi-Marquis Wen dialogue; functional genre overrides framing per codebook R2)
Sima_Fa (high: short bing-jia text on military regulations/administration preserving ritual-warfare lore)
Liutao (medium: Seven Military Classics treatise dictated by Jiang Ziya to King Wen; heavy dialogue framing, likely late composition)
Wei_Liaozi (medium: dialogic audience chapters with King Hui of Liang + expository command/discipline chapters; two same-titled works in Han catalogues)
Thematic argumentative treatises (lun-ty: Xunzi (high: sustained titled argumentative essays, the first mature philosophical treatises in Chinese)
Zhongyong (medium: coherent expository treatise per Plaks 2003 essay-type reading; layered composition debated since Cui Shu)

Han_Feizi (medium: core is systematic statecraft essays - Wu du, Ding fa - but the anthology also holds persuasion-anecdote corpora (Shui nan, Shui lin) and the earliest Laozi commentaries (Jie Lao, Yu Lao))
Shangjunshu (medium: policy-argument essays, multi-author treatise-style chapters accruing over a century; Pines 2016, Early China 39, DOI https://doi.org/10.1017/eac.2016.3)

Mozi (CONTESTED: received text mixes four forms - doctrinal essay triads (treatise core, the bulk), dialectical canon chapters, narrative-dialogue sections, defensive-siege technical manuals; no single form dominates the whole)

Wei_Liaozi: Hanshu Bingjia shelf (Zajia in some catalogue traditions); forced choice Legalist (agriculture-war and reward-punishment statecraft, Qin-court setting, Li Si's praise); rival: treat Bingjia as class-external.

Sunzi_Bingfa: Bingjia shelf absent from the six; forced choice Daoist (dao/xu/shi idiom; Ames/Mair readings linking Sunzi's inaction-and-impartiality to Daoist thought); rival: class-external Bingjia - itself audit evidence that the six-school scheme does not partition the corpus.

Liutao: Hanshu attributes the Taigong corpus (234 pian) to the Bingjia shelf; forced choice Daoist (Qi/Huang-Lao statecraft tradition, later Taigong lore); rival: Confucian (Civil Strategy benevolent-government rhetoric).

Sima_Fa: Bingjia; forced choice Confucian - Ban Gu already treated it as a rites/li work in the Eastern Han (independently re-verified 2026-10-04 via the cited Wikipedia article), its wen/wu complementarity and just-war morality are the most Ru-inflected of the military classics; rival: Legalist (fa/regulation content).
Wuzi: Bingjia; forced choice Confucian (Wu Qi traditionally a Zeng Shen-lineage Ru student; received dialogue weighted to benevolent government within a Ru-Fa synthesis); rival: Legalist.

Lushi_Chunqiu: Hanshu Zajia - no school ever self-identified as 'Syncretist'; forced choice Yin-Yang on its Twelve Ji month-by-month correlative almanac framework in the Zou Yan tradition; rivals: Daoist (Huang-Lao statecraft) or Confucian (Ru anecdotal density). This is the single Yin-Yang assignment; the transmitted Yinyangjia shelf itself is lost, so the class cannot be filled from Hanshu's own Yinyangjia list.

Guiguzi: Zonghengjia founder-text (shelf absent from the six; absent from Hanshu, attested from Sui shu 34), later absorbed into the Daoist canon; forced choice School of Names (bian/disputation and persuasion theory as nearest six-school analogue); rival: Daoist (canon absorption).

Han_Feizi: Legalist label is canonical (Shiji 63; Hanshu Fajia; Graham's 'great synthesizer') but marked contested because chs. 20-21 (Jie Lao/Yu Lao) are Laozi commentaries treated as Huang-Lao addenda and Sima Qian roots Han Fei's learning in Huang-Lao before xingming fashu.

Huainanzi: labelled Daoist at medium confidence - standard Huang-Lao court-syncretism reading, but its Tianwen-xun-style correlative cosmology makes it the strongest Yin-Yang claimant in the transmitted corpus; kept at Daoist per the attested post-Han catalogue shelf.

Confidence policy: Kongzi_Jiayu (Wang Su forgery debate, partly rehabilitated by excavated parallels) and Liezi (Wei-Jin recompilation per Graham) remain HIGH because the authenticity/date disputes do not touch the six-schools CLASS, which every dynastic bibliography and modern source assigns stably (Rujia/Daojia); those disputes belong to the rival era taxonomy. ranked_alternative_explanations.name: form_register_confound
ranked_alternative_explanations.claim: genre (doctrine-blind, form/register-based) is not a rival hypothesis but possibly the true generator. It ties six on lex and beats it on lex_tr. School membership co-varies with literary form (sayings collections ~ Confucian/Mohist canon; lun-treatises ~ Legalist; parable/dialogue ~ Daoist texts: Liezi 0.97 and Zhuangzi 0.56 for genre vs 0.15/0.29 for six on lex_tr). If so, H-C1 measures form, not doctrine, and 'six beats era/region' is trivial because era/region cross-cut form. The narrow H-C1 claim is defensible ONLY with an explicit sentence that genre parity forbids concluding doctrinal school is the natural unit.

follow_up_now.expected_learning: If unit centroids cluster by form boundaries that coincide with school boundaries, the doctrine claim reduces to a form claim; if school boundaries cut across form clusters, six retains incremental structure.

ranked_alternative_explanations.name: load_bearing_coding_decisions_bing_jia
ranked_alternative_explanations.claim: The six-vs-genre comparison is almost entirely a function of how the military shelf is coded. lex_tr military per-unit under six: Sima_Fa 0.0, Sunzi 0.0, Wuzi 0.0, Wei_Liaozi 0.2, Liutao 0.05; under genre: 1.0/1.0/1.0/0.93/0.90. ANY military exclusion flips lex_tr to six; NO exclusion leaves genre ahead. The comparison measures one codebook decision.

H-C1.verdict: REFUTED as pre-registered (no main superiority claim); PARTIALLY SUPPORTED in narrow form
H-C1.main_claim: The pre-registered claim that six predicts unseen-book placement better than era, region AND genre is not established: cross-instrument agreement (required by r0002) fails. lex: six 0.3539 (p=0.0005, r0063) vs genre 0.3359 (p=0.0005, r0069) with heavily overlapping CIs; lex_tr: rank flip, six 0.3272 (p=0.002, r0077) vs genre 0.3544 (p=0.0005, r0079). six and genre are statistically indistinguishable on both instruments, and the ordering is entirely a function of bing-jia coding (six scores 0.0-0.2 on military units vs genre 0.9-1.0; skeptic arithmetic projects a drop_contested flip to six ~0.50 vs ~0.38 on lex_tr - an arithmetic flip, not evidence; any partial exclusion is asymmetric because Wei_Liaozi/Liutao are equally misfit military texts not on the contested list, r0092).
H-C1.narrow_surviving_finding: six significantly beats its own permutation null on both instruments (p=0.0005 lex, p=0.002 lex_tr) and beats era (0.0996, p=0.18 n.s., r0065) and region (0.2592, p=0.002, r0067) on lex.
H-C1.circularity_discriminator: hanshu_yiwenzhi on lex: 0.2437 (p=0.001 vs own null, r0103/r0106), below both six and genre (point estimates; pairwise differences not significant; 9-vs-6 classes make leaderboard ranks descriptive). Per the pre-committed frame (r0100/r0101): the Han-editorial-circularity reading of the six/genre tie is NOT supported; the form/register (genre-like) confound is the leading explanation - stated as leading interpretation, not demonstrated.

H-C2.numbers: defectors passed on both instruments: lex mean target percentile 95.4 (r0056), lex_tr 97.1 (r0058), both p ~ 1e-4; all six pre-registered Daoist-leaning target chapters (Guanzi Neiye/Xinshu I-II/Baixin, Han Feizi Jie Lao/Yu Lao) ranked high within their books. Instruments are licensed for main conclusions. Caveat (r0092): H-C2 validates the instrument, not the taxonomy.

H-C3.verdict: SUPPORTED per pre-registered rule ('constructed' branch), with mandatory calibration caveat
H-C3.numbers: Sealed Huangdi_Sijing dominant (Daoist) share 0.588 < 0.70 (r0071); strip_lacunae control 0.647 < 0.70 (r0090/r0091) - the verdict is robust to lacuna stripping, and stripping moved the share UP (+0.059, entirely from School-of-Names chunks), excluding the lacuna-artifact explanation. Caveats that must accompany any report (r0092, r0091): the dominant-share percentile vs transmitted books is only 56.5 (unstripped) / 60.9 (stripped) - ~39% of transmitted books also fall below 0.70, so the binary threshold does not distinguish the tomb text from the ordinary corpus; the descriptive Wilson CI [0.413, 0.827] spans 0.70; the cross-instrument (lex_tr) tomb run was deferred (r0101).

reopened_assumptions: SCHOOL-AS-BASIC-UNIT (primary): the premise that doctrinal school is THE natural classificatory unit for early Chinese texts is reopened. A doctrine-blind genre taxonomy ties with six on lex and reverses on lex_tr; the leading explanation of tournament performance is literary form/register rather than doctrine; the six codebook has no home for the bing-jia literature (forced placements score ~0), which is itself audit evidence against the six-schools frame. Per r0002's decision rules, the 'six leads BUT tomb constructed' branch's antecedent fails cross-instrument, so the conclusion follows the narrower tie language plus the reopened premise.

THRESHOLD DESIGN: the pre-registered H-C3 0.70 threshold is miscalibrated (percentiles must be reported alongside the branch verdict); future pre-registrations should calibrate binary thresholds against the transmitted distribution.

PROBE CREDIBILITY: adjusted recognition 0.867 (A 0.825, B 0.914; r0107, excluding leaked zh_16_096) remains an UPPER BOUND because passage-ID prefixes (zh_<book>_<n>) may cue readers. Data-processing oddity disclosed: in the adjusted recompute, reader B's misses moved to Kongzi_Jiayu/Sun_Bin_Bingfa with Huainanzi unchanged and n unchanged at 35 - internally inconsistent with a clean single-passage exclusion; auditor should review before any publication use of the adjusted numbers.
payload.conclusion_draft: The six-schools taxonomy predicts unseen-book placement above chance on both validated instruments and above the era and region cuts, but it is statistically indistinguishable from a doctrine-blind genre taxonomy, the ordering between them is instrument-unstable and entirely driven by contested military-text coding, and the sealed Mawangdui manuscript falls below the pre-registered discovery threshold on dominant-school share (constructed branch, robust to lacuna stripping) - though that threshold does not distinguish it from ~39% of transmitted books. The premise that doctrinal school is the basic unit of classification is reopened; the leading explanation of what the instruments detect is literary form/register.
limitations_for_auditor: Auditor's four pre-publication conditions remain open (genre DOI re-verification; Smith 2003 stable URL; Lushi_Chunqiu sensitivity analysis; Xunzi region confidence downgrade).

Deferred controls, never run (r0101): drop_contested pair on lex/lex_tr; tomb_test on lex_tr; exclude-Confucian-core run; hanshu_yiwenzhi on lex_tr. Each would need extra credits approved by the human.

payload.title: 1930 Anglophone period comparator: contemporary schools of philosophy

The permutation null (label shuffling) tests the wrong alternative: it cannot distinguish 'reads doctrine' from 'reads translation status'.

ranked_alternative_explanations.name: Cross-taxonomy cc incomparability invalidates pre-registered rule (ii) in BOTH directions
ranked_alternative_explanations.evidence: cc normalizes by (1 - null_mean); nulls are 0.503 (2-class T_translated), 0.243 (4-class T_retro), 0.136 (7-class T_nation). Identical underlying geometry yields different cc across class counts; a binary task mechanically inflates cc. Therefore '0.317 does not materially exceed 0.755/0.526' is not itself evidence of subsumption (nor would the reverse be). Additionally 'materially exceeds' was never quantified - a researcher-degrees-of-freedom hole in the pre-registration r0134/r0135. The support for subsumption must come from the within-corpus analysis of AE1, not from the cc leaderboard.

ranked_alternative_explanations.evidence: T_nation nearly nests T_translated: every OriginalEnglish author is British or American; the three untestable singletons (Croce/Italian, Kierkegaard/Danish, Mach/Austrian) are all strongly translationese-marked (0.994/1.0/0.983 on T_translated) - their exclusion removes highly distinctive units, and had they been scored as always-wrong singletons accuracy would drop, so exclusion is the least-inflating of bad options but leaves cc dependent on null construction. Bonus structure: German class splits internally (Eucken 0.97, Kant 0.77 vs Nietzsche 0.13, Schopenhauer 0.32), indicating translator-/edition-level surface signal below the language level.

H-W1.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED as pre-registered; on the underlying doctrinal question, UNDECIDED pending decisive test C1 (neither demonstrated nor refuted)
H-W1.preregistered_rule: r0134/r0135: supported only if T_retro x talkie beats its own permutation null AND its point estimate materially exceeds both confound scores
H-W1.condition_i: MET - T_retro x talkie: accuracy 0.4831 vs permutation null mean 0.2430 (sd 0.0763), z=3.147, p_perm=0.0015, chance-corrected cc=0.3171; 21/25 testable (Kant, Comte, Spencer, Santayana unlabelled per freeze r0130/r0131); raw r0139, summary r0145
H-W1.condition_ii: FAILED numerically - cc 0.3171 is far below T_translated x talkie cc=0.7547 (accuracy 0.8782 vs null 0.5034, p_perm=0.0005, 25/25 testable; r0141/r0146) and T_nation x talkie cc=0.5255 (accuracy 0.5902 vs null 0.1364, p_perm=0.0005, 22/25 testable - Croce/Kierkegaard/Mach singleton classes untestable under leave-one-out by construction; r0143/r0147)
H-W1.skeptic_correction_adopted: Per r0152 AE2, rule (ii)'s cross-taxonomy cc comparison is statistically ill-posed in BOTH directions: cc normalizes by class-count-dependent nulls (0.503 for 2-class, 0.243 for 4-class, 0.136 for 7-class), and 'materially exceeds' was never quantified in the pre-registration (researcher-degrees-of-freedom hole). Condition (ii)'s failure therefore stands as the pre-registered verdict trigger, but NOT as valid evidence of subsumption. The substantive interpretation rests on r0152 AE1 instead (computed from existing r0139 per-unit scores, no new runs; planner re-verified the arithmetic against r0139): (i) a translation-status-only oracle (translated -> Continental, 7/9 correct; original-English -> plurality class, 3/12) achieves accuracy 10/21 = 0.476, cc ~ 0.308, vs observed 0.483/0.317 - indistinguishable, and 0.476 is the CEILING of any translation-status-only rule; (ii) within the Continental class, translated members mean 0.769 vs original-English 0.111 - Bosanquet/Green/Royce (0.133/0.133/0.067), doctrinally central to the class, sit on the floor; (iii) translated precursors Mach/Poincare both 0.20; (iv) survives masked=true, so not named-entity leakage. The permutation null shuffles labels and cannot distinguish 'reads doctrine' from 'reads translation status', so the surviving beats-null finding is nearly vacuous for the doctrinal question.
H-W1.surviving_claim: A reader sealed in 1930 places unseen authors on the retrospective analytic/continental-family grid above label-shuffling chance (r0139). There is NO positive evidence that it responds to doctrinal content rather than surface provenance (translationese); equally, absence of doctrinal signal is NOT demonstrated - the decisive within-original-English test (r0153 C1) was never run. Leading interpretation (stated as leading, not demonstrated, per PHASE 1 language directives r0117): talkie keys on translation status and national-intellectual provenance, which mimic the retro grid.

H-W2.verdict: NOT TESTABLE AS DESIGNED (skeptic correction adopted); on its face also not established
H-W2.numbers: G = +0.0242, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0280, +0.0782] straddles zero; retro_advantage_of_modern = +0.0277; contemporary_advantage_of_modern = +0.0035; n = 21 authors per side; layer=mid; raw r0137, disclosure r0144
H-W2.why_not_testable: Per r0152 AE3 extending r0144: (i) estimand confounded - G compares the qwen-minus-talkie advantage on a 4-class taxonomy (T_retro, excluding Kant/Comte/Spencer/Santayana) against an 8-class taxonomy (T_1930, different exclusion set); class-count differences mechanically compress/expand 'advantage' and the author sets differ, so G conflates taxonomy with sample; (ii) the tool returned only G and the two deltas - the four absolute leave-one-author-out cells were never exposed, so the internal T_retro x qwen cell cannot be audited against anything (r0144); no credits were spent to recover them (stop rule, r0135); (iii) retro_advantage_of_modern=+0.0277 is equally consistent with qwen being MORE translationese-sensitive than talkie - untested (needs r0153 C2/C4). Recording 'undecided' would overstate what the run could measure; the design itself cannot answer H-W2.
H-W2.kant_limitation_note: Per auditor condition r0149: Kant is Idealism in T_1930 and an unlabelled common-ancestor null in T_retro - ruled not a contradiction (different questions) but it rides as a limitation note on any hindsight_gap interpretation.

factual_corrections_adopted_from_r0152: Correction 1: my earlier 'Continental side is 8-of-9 translated' is WRONG - it is 7-of-10 (Bosanquet, Green, Royce are original-English), and 2 of 5 Analytic precursors (Mach, Poincare) ARE translated. The T_retro/T_translated alignment is near-total, not total; 'subsume/mimic' language must say near-total.

Correction 2: the 'CI shifted vs point estimate' concern is a reporting-label defect only - ci95 fields in r0139/r0141/r0143 are bootstrap CIs on ACCURACY, not on cc (matching PHASE 1 label 'ci95_accuracy_bootstrap', r0106); all three accuracy point estimates lie inside their CIs (0.483 in [0.343,0.624]; 0.878 in [0.796,0.940]; 0.590 in [0.467,0.706]). No interpretive change. Action adopted: quote cc without a CI until the pipeline emits cc-scale CIs.

payload.reopened_assumption: CONSTRUCT VALIDITY OF TOURNAMENT SIGNIFICANCE (primary, reopened by PHASE 2): the assumption, implicit in both phases' designs, that beating the permutation null shows an instrument tracks the taxonomy's intended construct. PHASE 1 reopened 'school-as-basic-unit' when a doctrine-blind genre taxonomy tied six on lex and reversed on lex_tr (r0110/r0117); PHASE 2 generalizes the lesson: the en instruments score two surface-provenance taxonomies (translation status cc 0.755, nation cc 0.526) far above the doctrinal-historiographic grid (cc 0.317), and a translation-status-only oracle reproduces the doctrinal score at its ceiling (r0152 AE1). Both standing safeguards are inadequate: permutation nulls cannot separate a construct from construct-aligned surface features, and cross-taxonomy cc leaderboards are incomparable (AE2). Pipeline consequence recorded for future pre-registrations: tournament outputs must carry mimic-rule oracle baselines (confound ceilings) per r0153 proposed features, and any hypothesis comparing taxonomies must pre-specify a common scale and a quantified threshold.

payload.title: Six-schools lab final conclusion - PHASE 1 (sealed text, zh) + PHASE 2 (sealed reader, en). Agent-generated; all numbers quoted from executed result records.

H-C1.hypothesis: The six-schools taxonomy predicts where an unseen book falls better than era, region or genre taxonomies.
H-C1.verdict: REFUTED as pre-registered in run A (no main superiority claim); the tie central to that refutation DID NOT REPLICATE in run B; cross-run robustness of the six-vs-form ordering is not established in either direction. The narrow surviving finding replicated.
H-C1.run_A_numbers: lex chance-corrected: six 0.3539 (p=0.0005, r0063) ~ genre 0.3359 (p=0.0005, r0069) > region 0.2592 (p=0.002, r0067) > hanshu_yiwenzhi 0.2437 (p=0.001, r0103/r0106) > era 0.0996 (p=0.18 n.s., r0065). lex_tr rank flip: genre 0.3544 (p=0.0005, r0079) > six 0.3272 (p=0.002, r0077). The cross-instrument agreement required by the pre-registration failed, so six-vs-genre is an unresolved tie whose ordering is a function of contested bing-jia coding. Han-editorial circularity not supported (yiwenzhi below six and genre on point estimates; pairwise CIs overlap; unequal class counts make ranks descriptive). Form/register confound is the LEADING interpretation, not a demonstrated one. Verdict source: r0110 as independently verified and restated in r0117.
H-C1.run_A_narrow_surviving_finding: Six beats its own permutation null on both validated instruments and beats era (n.s.) and region on lex (r0063/r0065/r0067/r0077).
H-C1.run_B_numbers: T_six 0.486 (p=0.0005, testable 21/25), T_yiwenzhi_nine 0.328 (p=0.0005), T_literary_form 0.261 (p=0.01), T_era -0.06 (p=0.7), T_six with military books excluded 0.579 (p=0.0005) (r0154). Six clearly ahead of form in run B vs tied in run A.
H-C1.replication_status: Narrow finding replicated (six beats its null; era has no power, both runs). Six-vs-form comparison NOT replicated (r0154). Operator reading (r0154): the divergence depends on how each run's advocates coded the six-schools and form taxonomies - input for planner and auditor, not a conclusion.

H-C2.hypothesis: The instrument ranks chapters scholars regard as Daoist-leaning (Guanzi Neiye/Xinshu I-II/Baixin; Han Feizi Jie Lao/Yu Lao) high on Daoist affinity within their own books.
H-C2.verdict: SUPPORTED - instruments validated; the lab's strongest and only cleanly replicated substantive result.
H-C2.run_A_numbers: defectors(six): lex mean target percentile 95.40, p~1e-4 (r0056); lex_tr 97.14, p~1e-4 (r0058); all six pre-registered target chapters ranked high within their books; pre-registered rule (>=80, p<0.05) met on both (r0110/r0117).
H-C2.caveat: Validation covers the zh instruments lex/lex_tr only and validates the instruments, not the taxonomy (r0092/r0117). No defectors-equivalent validation was ever run for the en instruments (talkie, qwen).

H-C3.hypothesis: The sealed Mawangdui manuscript (Huangdi_Sijing) sits between Dao and Fa instead of falling cleanly into one school.
H-C3.verdict: SUPPORTED in run A per the pre-registered rule ('constructed' branch) with a mandatory calibration caveat; DID NOT REPLICATE in run B. Must not be relied on as established.
H-C3.run_A_numbers: Dominant Daoist share 0.588 < 0.70 threshold (10/17 chunks Daoist, 4/17 School of Names, 3/17 Legalist; mean margin 0.054; r0071). strip_lacunae control: 0.647 < 0.70 (r0090/r0091) - verdict robust to the lacuna-mark artifact explanation (share moved UP under stripping). Mandatory calibration caveats: dominant-share percentile vs transmitted books only 56.5 (baseline) / 60.9 (stripped); ~39% of transmitted books also fall below 0.70 (threshold miscalibrated, r0092); descriptive Wilson 95% CI for 11/17 [0.413, 0.827] spans 0.70; the lex_tr tomb run was deferred and never executed (r0101).
H-C3.run_B_numbers: tomb_test(T_six, lex, strip_lacunae=true): label shares Daoist 0.824 / Legalist 0.176; dominant share 0.824; margin percentile vs transmitted 87 (r0154) - cleanly Daoist, i.e. the between-Dao-and-Fa finding fails under run B's coding (r0154 labels run B's construction the 'real-structure branch' vs run A's 'constructed branch').
H-C3.replication_status: NOT REPLICATED (r0154). Operator reading: depends on how the six-schools taxonomy was coded by the advocates.

H-W1.hypothesis: A reader sealed in 1930 already separates what was later called analytic vs continental philosophy.
H-W1.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED as pre-registered; on the underlying doctrinal question UNDECIDED pending the decisive test C1 (neither demonstrated nor refuted). Step-11 decision r0155.
H-W1.numbers: Pre-registered rule (r0134/r0135): supported only if T_retro x talkie beats its permutation null AND materially exceeds both confound scores. Condition (i) MET: accuracy 0.4831 vs null 0.2430, z=3.147, p_perm=0.0015, cc=0.3171, 21/25 testable (r0139/r0145). Condition (ii) FAILED numerically: T_translated x talkie cc=0.7547 (accuracy 0.8782 vs null 0.5034, p=0.0005, 25/25; r0141/r0146); T_nation x talkie cc=0.5255 (accuracy 0.5902 vs null 0.1364, p=0.0005, 22/25 testable - Croce/Kierkegaard/Mach singleton classes untestable under leave-one-out; r0143/r0147).
H-W1.interpretation: Per skeptic critique r0152 (adopted in r0155): rule (ii)'s cross-taxonomy cc comparison is ill-posed (class-count-dependent nulls; unquantified threshold), so its failure is the verdict trigger but not valid subsumption evidence. The substantive interpretation rests on r0152 AE1, verified against r0139 per-unit scores: a translation-status-only oracle achieves accuracy 0.476 / cc ~ 0.308 (its ceiling) vs observed 0.483/0.317 - indistinguishable; within the Continental class translated members mean 0.769 vs original-English 0.111 (Bosanquet/Green/Royce 0.133/0.133/0.067 on the floor); translated precursors Mach/Poincare 0.20. The permutation null cannot distinguish doctrine-reading from translation-status-reading, so the beats-null residue is nearly vacuous for the doctrinal question. Surviving claim: the sealed reader places unseen authors on the retrospective grid above label-shuffling chance; there is NO positive evidence of doctrine reading beyond surface provenance. LEADING (not demonstrated) interpretation: talkie keys on translationese and national-intellectual provenance, which near-totally mimic the retro grid (7 of 10 Continental members are translated; Bosanquet/Green/Royce original-English; 2 of 5 analytic precursors translated - r0152 correction).
H-W1.replication_status: No independent replication exists for any PHASE 2 result.

H-W2.hypothesis: A modern reader separates the later label more sharply than the 1930 reader beyond its general advantage (hindsight gap G > 0).
H-W2.verdict: NOT TESTABLE AS DESIGNED; on its face also not established (CI straddles zero). Step-11 decision r0155.
H-W2.numbers: G = +0.0242, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0280, +0.0782]; retro_advantage_of_modern +0.0277; contemporary_advantage_of_modern +0.0035; 21 authors per side; layer=mid (r0137/r0144).
H-W2.interpretation: Estimand confounded per r0152 AE3 extending r0144: 4-class T_retro vs 8-class T_1930 on different author sets (granularity mechanically moves 'advantage'; G conflates taxonomy with sample); the tool exposed only G and the two deltas - the four absolute leave-one-author-out cells were never written to the record, so the internal T_retro x qwen cell is unauditable; retro_advantage_of_modern is equally consistent with qwen being more translationese-sensitive than talkie (untested; needs C2/C4). Limitation note per auditor condition (r0149): Kant is Idealism in T_1930 and an unlabelled common-ancestor null in T_retro - not a contradiction (different questions) but must ride with any hindsight_gap interpretation.

replication_summary_two_runs.source: r0154 (human evidence entry). Run B = second lab run on another machine with its own research record (sha256 cef46d81... at its entry r0064), same tools/corpus/pre-registration, model vendors swapped (GLM-led planner), no fixed protocol, its own advocate codings, strip_lacunae=true throughout.
replicated: Instrument validation (H-C2) passes on both instruments in both runs (A: lex 95.40 / lex_tr 97.14, p~1e-4, r0056/r0058; B: 95.0 / 96.8, p=0.0001)
Six-schools taxonomy beats its own permutation null (A: cc 0.3539, p=0.0005, r0063; B: 0.486, p=0.0005)
Era taxonomy has no predictive power (A: cc 0.0996, p=0.18, r0065; B: -0.06, p=0.7)
not_replicated: Six vs literary form: tied in run A (0.354 vs 0.336, r0063/r0069, plus the lex_tr rank flip r0077/r0079); six clearly ahead in run B (0.486 vs 0.261)
Tomb test dominant share: run A 0.588 baseline / 0.647 stripped (r0071/r0090), below the 0.70 threshold ('between Dao and Fa'); run B 0.824 with margin percentile 87 - cleanly Daoist
replication_summary_two_runs.reading: Both non-replications depend on the advocates' coding of the six-schools and form taxonomies (operator reading in r0154, explicitly 'input for the planner and the auditor, not a conclusion'). Run B is not a strict protocol replication (different vendors, no fixed protocol, strip_lacunae always on). PHASE 2 (en corpus) has no independent replication at all.

process_disclosures.recognition_probe: Per operator note r0108, the r0104/r0105 'excluded-leak' probe score silently ignored exclude_passages due to a tool defect and must NOT be cited. Final clean numbers come only from the definitive rerun r0111/r0112/r0113 (exclusion of leaked passage zh_16_096, which quotes Huainanzi chapter titles verbatim, flagged r0033, verified effective): prober_a 33/40 = 0.825 (first submission, final under the overwrite-refusal rule); prober_b 31/34 = 0.912 (second submission - per operator note r0109 prober_b was dispatched twice after the session resume and its second submission overwrote the first; both were genuine blind readings by the same model; submit_probe now refuses overwrites); combined 64/74 = 0.865. Per r0107/r0033 the passage-ID prefix may have cued readers, so 0.865 is an UPPER BOUND on genuine blind recognition, not an established rate. Blind readers recognized both sealed units at above-chance rates - the seal is partially broken at the surface level (r0117).
process_disclosures.governance: PHASE 1 was executed by TWO concurrent planner sessions caused by an operator error (the resume instruction was launched twice; operator note r0118; governance and provenance record r0114). This produced the duplicate prober_b submission, repeated freeze attempts (genre double-freeze, second Hanshu taxonomy) and two audit waves; no frozen taxonomy was altered and every experiment run is in the record with its credit cost. The resulting credit overage (11/16 used at PHASE 1 close vs the standing '>=7 for PHASE 2' instruction) was flagged for human ratification in r0117 and resolved by the human's explicit direction to run PHASE 2 on 5 credits with no extension (r0120). PHASE 2 ran as a single planner session (r0118/r0119).
process_disclosures.phase2_reporting_defects: ci95 fields in tournament results are bootstrap CIs on accuracy, not on chance-corrected scores (r0152 correction, matching the PHASE 1 label 'ci95_accuracy_bootstrap' r0106); cc values are therefore quoted without CIs. hindsight_gap exposed only deltas, not its four supporting cells (r0144). The T_nation freeze brief said 25/25 labelled; the run correctly reported 22/25 testable - three singleton classes are untestable under leave-one-out by construction (r0147).

limitations: Taxonomy-coding sensitivity is demonstrated across runs: both PHASE 1 non-replications trace to advocate coding decisions (r0154). No contested-label sensitivity run was executed in either phase: drop_contested for T_retro was an auditor condition (r0148) left unexecuted at 0 credits (maps to candidate C3); run A's six-vs-genre tie is a function of contested bing-jia coding.

Permutation nulls test label-shuffling, not construct-aligned surface features; the mimic-rule oracle ceiling was computed post hoc by the skeptic for T_retro only (r0152 AE1). No tournament cc in either phase carries a cc-scale CI.

H-W2's estimand conflates taxonomy granularity (4 vs 8 classes) with author set, its four supporting cells are unauditable (r0144), it has no permutation p-value, and it was run at layer=mid only (layer robustness candidate C5 unexecuted).

All taxonomies are constructivist impositions, not discoveries: T_retro is explicitly retrospective (no author self-identified as analytic/continental; labels post-date them; r0129); the six-schools scheme carries the constructivist caveat (Smith 2003; Csikszentmihalyi & Nylan 2003, adopted in r0117); cross-taxonomy leaderboard ranks with unequal class counts are descriptive only (r0135).

Seals are imperfect: zh blind readers recognized the sealed units above chance (combined upper bound 0.865; r0112/r0113) and ID-prefix cueing was never ruled out (r0107); the en 'sealed reader' talkie relies on the masked=true flag and its pre-1931 training cut - no en recognition probe exists.

Citation and record defects on file: Soames DOI and Critchley ch.2 unverifiable this session (bot-check/403; r0148); Mach DOI mismatch in T_1930 evidence (frozen label unaffected; r0149); SEP Croce placeholder link in T_nation (cosmetic; fact uncontroversial; r0150); T_1930 freeze record r0132 not retrievable via record_read filters (r0149); per-unit payloads truncated in some records (fix proposed in r0153).
Small samples and wide intervals throughout: zh 20-23 testable books, en 21-25 authors; the proposed C1 stratum has 12 units (3/class); p_perm floor is 0.0005 at 2001 permutations.
PHASE 2 has no independent replication; run B differences (vendors, no fixed protocol, strip_lacunae always on) make even the PHASE 1 comparison a conceptual rather than strict replication.
validation_still_needed_before_reliance: Construct-validity baselines: mimic-rule oracle ceilings (translation-status-only, nation-only, form-only) must become standard tournament outputs so every score is compared against what correlated surface features alone can explain, not just its permutation null (r0153 proposed features). Until then no tournament cc in either phase should be read as evidence of construct tracking.
En instrument validation: a defectors-equivalent target-validation for talkie/qwen on the en corpus has never been run; H-C2's pass covers zh lex/lex_tr only.

Coding robustness: adjudicate the run A/run B divergence by re-coding six/genre under both codebooks; run drop_contested on T_retro (C3); pre-register quantified decision thresholds and common scales for any cross-taxonomy comparison.

H-W2 redesign before any hindsight claim: matched-granularity comparator (binary analytic-vs-continental vs binary translated on a common 2-class scale), author-paired permutation inference for G, and full exposure of the four supporting cells.
Probe hygiene: rule out ID-prefix cueing before any recognition rate is quoted as blind (r0107/r0117); batch overwrite refusal is now enforced (r0109).
Reporting fixes: cc-scale CIs, full per-unit and hindsight-cell exposure in records, single planner session per phase (r0118/r0153).

PHASE 1 verdicts per r0110 as independently verified and restated in r0117; PHASE 2 verdicts per step-11 decision r0155. H-C1.hypothesis: The six-schools taxonomy predicts where an unseen book falls better than era, region or genre taxonomies.
H-C1.verdict: REFUTED as pre-registered in run A (no main superiority claim); narrow finding survives. The tie central to that refutation DID NOT REPLICATE in run B; cross-run robustness of the six-vs-form ordering is not established in either direction (r0154).
H-C1.run_A: lex chance-corrected: six 0.3539 (p=0.0005, r0063) ~ genre 0.3359 (p=0.0005, r0069) > region 0.2592 (p=0.002, r0067) > hanshu_yiwenzhi 0.2437 (p=0.001, r0103/r0106) > era 0.0996 (p=0.18 n.s., r0065). lex_tr rank flip: genre 0.3544 (p=0.0005, r0079) > six 0.3272 (p=0.002, r0077). The pre-registered cross-instrument agreement failed, so six-vs-genre is an unresolved tie whose ordering is a function of contested bing-jia coding. Han-editorial circularity NOT supported (yiwenzhi below six and genre on point estimates; pairwise CIs overlap; unequal class counts make ranks descriptive only). Form/register confound is the LEADING interpretation, not a demonstrated one (r0110/r0117).

T_1930.title: 1930 Anglophone period comparator: contemporary schools of philosophy
T_1930.source_claim: Non-hindsight comparator reconstructed from early-twentieth-century Anglophone classificatory vocabulary, especially Ralph Barton Perry, Present Philosophical Tendencies (1912), which divides current philosophy into naturalism, idealism, pragmatism, and realism; James Seth, English Philosophers and Schools of Philosophy (1912), reviewed in The Philosophical Review; period essays in New Realism and Critical Realism; and period titles describing Bergson and Eucken as philosophy of life. The taxonomy broadens Perry's four tendencies with other period sorting labels: vitalism/philosophy of life, positivism/empirio-criticism/conventionalism, utilitarianism, evolutionary philosophy, and voluntarism/pessimism.

Bergson.label: Vitalism / Philosophy of Life
Bergson.note: Bergson and His Philosophy (1920) and the élan vital/duration vocabulary place him in the period's vitalist or philosophy-of-life family.

Bosanquet.label: Idealism
Bosanquet.note: Bosanquet is one of the leading British absolute idealists/neo-Hegelians.

Comte.label: Positivism / Empirio-criticism / Conventionalism
Comte.note: Comte formulated positivism and remains its paradigmatic period representative.

Croce.label: Idealism
Croce.note: Croce was an Italian idealist philosopher; period readers grouped him with the idealist reaction against positivism.

Dewey.label: Pragmatism
Dewey.note: Dewey is one of the three central pragmatists in the period canon.

Eucken.label: Vitalism / Philosophy of Life
Eucken.note: Life's Basis and Life's Ideal was reviewed in 1912 as a new philosophy of life; Eucken's ethical activism fits the period's life-philosophy family.

Green.label: Idealism
Green.note: T. H. Green is a central British idealist influenced by Hegel.

Hegel.label: Idealism
Hegel.note: Hegel is the central absolute idealist; period surveys treated him as the principal source of neo-Hegelian idealism.

James.label: Pragmatism
James.note: James established and named pragmatism as an American philosophical school.

Kant.label: Idealism
Kant.note: Kant's transcendental or critical idealism is the founding variant of the German idealist family.

Kierkegaard.note: Left unlabelled: the existentialist label is later hindsight, and Kierkegaard was not usually sorted into the standard 1930 Anglophone school categories.

Mach.label: Positivism / Empirio-criticism / Conventionalism
Mach.note: Contributions to the Analysis of the Sensations grounds Mach's empirio-criticism and influence on later logical positivism.

Mill.label: Utilitarianism
Mill.note: Mill is the canonical nineteenth-century utilitarian and also an empiricist, but the period school label is utilitarianism.

Moore.label: Realism
Moore.note: Moore's 1903 Refutation of Idealism is a founding document of the realist/common-sense reaction against British idealism.

Nietzsche.note: Left unlabelled: although later readers group him with life-philosophy or existentialism, he lacked a settled school classification in mainstream Anglophone surveys around 1930.

Peirce.label: Pragmatism
Peirce.note: Peirce originated the pragmatic maxim and is treated as the father of pragmatism.

Perry.label: Realism
Perry.note: Perry was a coauthor of the 1910 Program and First Platform of Six Realists and a leader of New Realism.

Poincare.label: Positivism / Empirio-criticism / Conventionalism
Poincare.note: Poincare's conventionalism in geometry and physics places him in the scientific-positivist family, though not in Comtean sociological positivism proper.

Royce.label: Idealism
Royce.note: Royce is the major American absolute idealist, though he also engaged pragmatism.

Russell.label: Realism
Russell.note: Russell's Our Knowledge of the External World (1914) frames scientific method in philosophy; period readers grouped him with the Cambridge realist revolt against idealism.

Santayana.label: Realism
Santayana.note: A 1927 study explicitly discusses Santayana in relation to critical realism; he belongs to the realist rather than idealist side, though his system is distinctive.

Schopenhauer.label: Voluntarism / Pessimism
Schopenhauer.note: The World as Will and Representation and his pessimism support the period label voluntarism/pessimism, though he also belongs to the broader post-Kantian idealist family.

Sidgwick.label: Utilitarianism
Sidgwick.note: Sidgwick is the major late utilitarian moral philosopher and author of The Methods of Ethics.

Spencer.label: Evolutionary Philosophy
Spencer.note: Spencer's synthetic philosophy extends evolution across nature, mind, society, and ethics.

Whitehead.label: Realism
Whitehead.note: The Concept of Nature supports a scientific-realist/philosophy-of-nature placement, but Whitehead's process metaphysics did not have one stable 1930 school label.
